title: Microsoft restoring services after a worldwide outage
summary: Outlook, Teams and other services failed in dozens of countries. The company says it was not a cyberattack.
body:
Microsoft says it is gradually restoring its services after an outage that disrupted email, Teams and other products around the world.

The problems began on Thursday 12 November. Within an hour, users in more than 70 countries had reported faults, and banks, government offices, health services, railways and courts were among those affected.

What went wrong

Microsoft said a large number of its servers became unavailable after a process that sets up secure connections was overwhelmed. A company executive said the outage was not caused by a security breach.

On Friday the company said traffic was returning and that email was approaching normal levels, though recovery was not yet complete. This explanation is preliminary, and Microsoft has not yet published a full report.

Sources: CNN, RTÉ, ABC News (Australia).
